text:
maria huang: CI alert on PR 18502 — microperf benchmark exceeded thresholds.
ci-bot: [perf-check] Failure in job `microbench-kernel` (ref: refs/pull/18502/head). Failing tests:
- bench_kernel_selector::test_kv_hit_rate (delta: -6.2%)
- bench_batch_latency::p95 (delta: +12%)
Artifacts: https://ci.internal/redwood/job/18502/artifacts/
sam choi: ugh, kv_hit_rate down 6% is pretty big. any obvious change in this PR? short diff looked like kernel-cost tweaks and a tiny batching heuristic change.
priya nanda: I ran the microbench locally against that branch with --bench-seed=42. Reproduced kv hit drop and tail increase. Heap profile shows extra work in choose_kernel during warmup.
jon taylor: can you paste the flamegraph/snippet? is it allocation or CPU hot path?
priya nanda: snippet below from pprof (collapsed):
```
choose_kernel  48.3%
  compute_costs  31.2%
    compute_attention_cost  18.5%
kv_cache_lookup  4.1%
batch_scheduler::wait_for_batch  6.0%
```
Top line points to kernel_selector loop calling compute_costs per candidate.
liwei zhang: that smells like the new cost model makes the selector iterate more candidates instead of short-circuiting. I pushed a comment in the PR about early-exit.
maria huang: PR diff includes 1) cost model change (commit a1f9c2b) and 2) a change to batcher sampling weight (commit b2d0e3f). Which one is root cause?
sam choi: quickest path: bisect between before a1f9c2b and after b2d0e3f. I can run a bisect on CI if someone gives the commit range. Plan: run microbench on each step with the perf job config.
jon taylor: also run with KV_HIT_METRICS=1 env to see cache hit breakdown. If the selector is changing sequence lengths chosen, kv hit could drop because prefixes differ.
priya nanda: ran git bisect locally:
```
git bisect start HEAD a1f9c2b~1
git bisect run ./tools/run_microbench.sh --bench filter=kernel_selector
```
Result: a1f9c2b is the first bad commit. It adjusts candidate scoring to prefer smaller-launch kernels.
sam choi: nice. so cost model change is culprit. Does that explain the tail latency increase? maybe more frequent kernel switches causing cold path overhead.
liwei zhang: yep. I can craft a short patch to restore the early-exit heuristic and run bench. If that fixes, we should revert a1f9c2b from main until we ship a refined cost model.
maria huang: hold merge and mark rollout blocker. @eng-release please pause merge queue. :warning:
ci-bot: Merge queue pause requested by maria huang for PR 18502. Status: blocked.
sam choi: quick experiment: I applied a revert on top of the PR and ran the microbench — kv_hit_rate back to baseline within noise (delta -0.2%). p95 back to +1%.
jon taylor: sounds like revert is safe plan. liwei, can you open a short revert PR and tag it as urgent? we should include the microbench diff and the bisect notes in the description.
liwei zhang: on it. I'll include reproducer flags and bench commands. Also adding a unit test to guard the early-exit behavior so future cost tweaks don't regress.
priya nanda: leaving the artifacts link in the revert PR: https://ci.internal/redwood/job/18502/artifacts/bench-results.html
maria huang: thanks all. after revert lands we'll rerun the whole perf job and unpause if green. Follow-up: design doc for cost-model changes before any more kernel scoring changes.
sam choi: ACK. I'll create the doc template and assign reviewers from eng-runtime + eng-ml.
maria huang: closing loop — tagging @release and @pm for visibility. :+1:
